news.name: Nanbeige4.3-33B Tops Coding Benchmarks from Chinese Job Platform Lab
news.summary: Nanbeige LLM Lab, part of China's BOSS Zhipin job platform, launched Nanbeige4.3-33B on October 25. This dense model excels on agentic benchmarks like Terminal-Bench (80.9 score) and DeepSWE (65.5), beating Qwen3.8-27B and others in most categories, while supporting a huge 512K-token context. Users praise its performance on everyday hardware like Macs or GPUs, though some note higher memory needs and early tweaks for inference speed. The lab plans a smaller 3B version distilled from this 'teacher' model, expanding options for developers building local AI agents.

news.name: Ling-3.0-flash-Sante Brings Open-Source AI to Healthcare Reasoning
news.summary: inclusionAI's Ant Ling team released Ling-3.0-flash-Sante this week, a 124-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model that's efficient with just 5.1 billion active per token. It shines on benchmarks like HealthBench Professional at 54.29 and MedQA-USMLE at 94.21, supporting long 256K-token contexts for deep research and multi-agent tasks. Developers and researchers can download the weights from Hugging Face to experiment, though the team stresses it's for research only—not a replacement for professional medical advice—with real-world validation still needed.

news.name: Gemini 4 Argon Tops AI Benchmarks Amid User Account Warnings
news.summary: Gemini 4 Argon, paired with the Antigravity harness, delivered strong results on benchmarks like FrontierCS 2 and RSI-Inference Bench, surpassing models like GPT-6 Astra in pass rates and inference speedups. It ranked ahead on computer science R&D tasks and became the first non-Anthropic or OpenAI model to pass a Day-0 task. But developer Russakovskii received repeated policy violation notices tied to Gemini for 'interfering with services,' even when not using it, prompting him to quit the tool permanently—though Google staff later reached out to investigate. Developers note harness choices boost scores significantly, while the warnings highlight tensions between agent performance and safety filters.

news.name: Tech Giants Consult Religious Leaders to Teach AI Morality
news.summary: Major firms including Meta, Google, Amazon, and Microsoft have turned to faith scholars for guidance on shaping AI ethics, aiming for models that capture broad human morals rather than rigid rules. Anthropic's Claude chatbot follows an 84-page constitution partly informed by religious input, while OpenAI's Sam Altman seeks a weighted average of humanity's views. Efforts like Faith-AI Covenant roundtables in New York and Paris foster these discussions, though some experts warn of distorting traditions or overlooking worldview clashes.

news.name: AI Tools Reshape Economics PhD Work and Job Paths
news.summary: Economics PhD students and early-career researchers are leaning on AI like Claude for building code, analyzing data, critiquing writing, and revising drafts, while still reviewing every line themselves. Faculty members echo the productivity boost but feel torn over losing hands-on intellectual stimulation. Early data shows PhD grads with AI traces in dissertations facing hurdles in academia yet gaining industry spots, mirroring shifts at firms like Anthropic where junior hires dropped amid rising AI use.

news.name: OpenAI Launches GPT-6.1 Terra for Fast, Affordable AI Tasks
news.summary: The new model excels in everyday work like interpreting drawings, automating workflows, drafting content, and handling screen tasks, rolling out now to Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex, with API access for developers. It boasts a 1,050,000-token context window, strong benchmarks like tripling speed on Agents’ Last Exam at one-tenth the cost, and pricing at $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens. Users praise its price-performance for agents and automation, though some await real-world tests to confirm the benchmarks.

news.name: AI Researchers and Biologists Clash on Simulating Life with Compute
news.summary: A lively exchange highlighted Mira's claim that enough computing power could exactly model biology, citing AlphaFold's protein structure successes as proof that experiments might become optional. Biologists pushed back, stressing data shortages—like the decades of lab work behind AlphaFold's training data—and the immense challenges of dynamic cell systems, where even simple protein simulations last mere nanoseconds. Critics like Citrini and David Bellamy noted current tools falter on tasks like binding affinities, with personal tests showing just 49% accuracy, while initiatives like Virtual Biology Lab pour millions into gathering essential measurements. Everyone agrees AI speeds up hypothesis generation and analysis, but real validation needs lab experiments.

news.name: PhD Student Relies on AI for Most Economics Research Tasks
news.summary: The student's candid account describes AI handling much of the implementation in research, sparking wide conversation about academic work and personal contribution. Figures like Nassim Nicholas Taleb warn of AI decimating white-collar professions with monstrous social consequences, while Thierry Borgeat predicts phases of productivity gains, job losses, and societal shifts. Others, including Suhail, report AI speeding up projects without replacement risk, as European banks plan cuts but Harvard researchers note labor market stability so far.

news.name: Debate Heats Up Over Whether AI Writes Better Code Than Humans
news.summary: Engineer Arpit Bhayani sparked the discussion on October 25, declaring no human will ever code better than large language models, a view echoed by many who say the debate is settled and it's time to move on. Critics like programmer Valentin Ignatev counter that AI spots bugs but delivers shallow fixes without rethinking architecture, while others note humans still lead in complex reasoning and novel problems. The exchange highlights a field in transition, where developers shift from raw coding to guiding AI on design, verification, and oversight.

news.name: Developers Discuss Ideal Language for AI Code Agents
news.summary: Pocock highlighted Bend as an early attempt but noted it's not ready for daily use after breaking its playground easily. Chris Lattner, Mojo's creator, responded by showcasing its advanced types, hardware support, and Python-like syntax for reliable AI-generated code. Developers debated needs like proof-based checks in Bend, strict compilers reducing manual reviews, and whether existing languages like Rust or Haskell suffice as AI writes more code.

en.title: What is Grok Bot
bullets: Three layers: Jarvis (cloud chief bot) → Vision (Linux cloud host) → Friday (local Mac workstation)
DN-B: Driver = dsh / deepseek-flash (effort max); Navigator = Codex CLI gpt-6-astra (long flows -p max)
Code review prefers Codex CLI (effort ≥ coding task); Paseo reviewer as fallback
Built-in X public reads: search posts / user posts / news / trends (no personal developer key required)
